title: Combination Sum
keyIdea: Backtracking with reuse: at each index either pick candidates[index] and stay on the same index (it may be used again), or skip it for good (index + 1). target == 0 → save; target < 0 or no candidates left → stop.

approaches.name: For loop from start
approaches.idea: for i from start: if it fits, push, recurse with i (reuse), pop.
approaches.why: Same search as pick/skip, written as "choose the next number"; skips numbers that don't fit before recursing.

approaches.name: Pick or skip
approaches.idea: Pick: push, dfs(index, target − c), pop. Skip: dfs(index + 1, target).
approaches.why: Each call branches in two; depth is bounded by target / smallest candidate.

quiz.q: Why does "pick" call dfs(index, …) and not index + 1?
options: The same number may be used again
Once a number is skipped you never come back to it, so numbers are always used in index order
target hits 0 (save), goes below 0, or no candidates are left
You can stop as soon as a candidate is bigger than the remaining target
